title: The Electric Seaglider That Flies on Air
summary:
It's a bird! It's a plane! Actually, it's a 50-foot-long electric seaglider. Built by Regent Craft, it can float like a boat, rise on hydrofoils, and fly above the water at up to 180 miles per hour.

The trick is the ground effect: flying close to water gives an aircraft extra lift and less drag. 'We're flying on a cushion of air,' says company founder Billy Thalheimer.

It can travel up to 180 miles on one charge. The bigger passenger craft, Viceroy, first flew this September and can carry up to 14 people. Thalheimer says it could be six times faster than a ferry, but half the cost of a plane ticket.

In July 2016, Thalheimer and Mike Klinker entered a contest to fly human-powered machines over water, and their craft nosedived into Boston's Charles River. 'The flight went horrendously wrong,' Thalheimer says, 'but it was also a really good lesson.'

A jet engine has thousands of parts, but the seaglider's battery has no moving parts and its motor has one. Both craft passed their float, foil, and fly tests.
why_it_matters: A fast, cheap electric craft could change how you travel across bays and between islands one day.

keywords.explanation: A seaglider is a craft that floats like a boat and flies just above the water.
Hydrofoils are wing-like parts under a boat that lift it up out of the water as it moves.
Ground effect is the extra lift an aircraft gets when it flies very close to the water or ground.
Drag is the force of air or water that slows a moving craft down.
Viceroy is the name of the bigger passenger seaglider that can carry up to 14 people.

background_read: A seaglider is a new kind of electric craft that floats like a boat, rises on wing-like parts called hydrofoils, and then flies just above the water.
Flying close to the water gives it extra lift, which is called the ground effect.
Electric motors have far fewer moving parts than jet engines, so the craft is simpler to build and run.
